# Artifact Keeper 1.12.0

A large minor release: 328 changelog entries across about 300 merged pull requests since 1.11.3. The headline additions are an **MCP Registry** repository format with Local, Remote and Virtual registries, capability introspection in an isolated sandbox, and lint (#5253), hosted **Agent Plugins** repositories for coding-agent plugin marketplaces (#5251, #5289), and **disconnected operation**: cache-only Remotes, proxy-cache seeding, an upstream-fetch audit trail, one switch that pauses every job that contacts an upstream, an offline scanner adapter with a vulnerability DB import route, and repository config export and import (#5282, #5284, #5286, #5288, #5287, #5292). Around them: scan-on-proxy for ten more formats (Go, RubyGems, Composer, Pub, Conan, CocoaPods, Swift, Debian, RPM, Alpine; #4103 to #4113), durable finding acknowledgements (#5153), the RFC 8628 device authorization grant (#3461), LDAP/AD credentials for package-manager clients (#3830), `<NAME>_FILE` secret mounts (#4142), logs and metrics over OTLP (#4337), hosted conda repodata rendered once per change with stored CEP-16 shards and real JLAP (#4173, #4174, #4175), precomputed hosted RPM repodata (#4544), a proxy-cache size cap and Azure-hosted proxy cache (#4660, #4320), repository deletes run as background jobs (#4311), and a hosted Terraform origin registry (#4356). The rest is security and correctness work, most of it on the MCP registry, proxies and virtual repositories. This page groups the highlights; the `## [1.12.0]` section of `CHANGELOG.md` has every entry.

1.12.0 also contains every fix shipped on the 1.11 line after 1.11.3. If you are upgrading from **1.11.12**, 85 of these entries are already deployed (1.11.4 to 1.11.12), and 9 more are also in **1.11.13**: the jemalloc allocator (#5130), cancelled proxy fills that still fill the cache (#5220), the held-path release during a fetch (#5223), the inconclusive-scan `423` reason (#5473), bounded proxy database connections (#5475), `503` instead of `401` on a database outage (#5476), the multibyte token-prefix panic (#5525), scan findings with long version strings (#5534, migration 339) and the grype / buildctl rebuild (#5565).

## Upgrade notes

Read this block before upgrading. **A rolling upgrade from 1.11.x is supported**; no migration in this release needs every old replica stopped first. The caveats for a mixed 1.11/1.12 fleet are listed below.

- **Upgrade the web UI with the backend: backend 1.12.0 needs artifact-keeper-web 1.12.0 or later** (#5663). Web 1.11.x shows an error page on the repository listing and on every Remote or Virtual repository page against backend 1.12.0, because package listings now report `download_count: null` for Remote and Virtual Maven packages where the count is unknown (#5419).
- **Upgrade the `ak` CLI to 1.11.0 or later.** ak 1.2.0 and earlier report an error on `ak repo delete` against 1.12.0 although the delete succeeded, because the route now answers `202` with a job (#4311, see below).

### Migrations

**Upgrading to 1.12.0 from any of 1.11.3 through 1.11.11 runs 51 migrations** (290 to 341; 332 was never used). From 1.11.12 it runs 50, because 330 shipped there; from 1.11.13, 49, because 339 shipped there too under the same number. Most are additive tables and columns. The ones to plan for:

- **339 changes six `scan_findings` columns to `TEXT`** (#5534). On PostgreSQL 16 and later it is a catalog-only change (no table rewrite, no index rebuild) that briefly takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on `scan_findings`, waiting at most 5 seconds per attempt and retrying, and drops and recreates the `scan_findings_effective` view in the same transaction.
  - **If every lock attempt times out (about 35 seconds, for example behind a long-running transaction on `scan_findings`), the migration fails and the server exits at startup.** Nothing is left half-applied, and the next start retries it. Make sure no long transaction holds `scan_findings` when the first 1.12.0 replica starts.
  - **Rolling-upgrade caveat: replicas still on the previous version fail findings reads after 339 has run** (findings list, policy evaluation, SBOM). A pooled connection that prepared a findings query before the migration keeps failing until the replica is replaced or the connection reaches its 1800-second maximum lifetime. Measured under load, the window on old replicas lasted 29 minutes and about 97% of their findings-list reads failed in it. Clients see `500 {"code":"DATABASE_ERROR","message":"Database operation failed"}`; the PostgreSQL error `cached plan must not change result type` appears only in the server log. Replace the old replicas promptly after the first new one has migrated.
- **340 lets a peer delete outlive the artifact row** (#5624): the `sync_tasks.artifact_id` foreign key becomes `ON DELETE SET NULL` (it cascaded), three nullable target columns record the repository id, key and path each delete task removes on the peer, and unfinished delete tasks are backfilled. The columns are catalog-only (nullable, no default) and the new foreign key is added `NOT VALID`, so nothing is rewritten or scanned for validation. The swap takes `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` on `sync_tasks` and `artifacts` together, in the order the application uses, and holds both through the backfill (about 15 µs per unfinished delete task). Measured on a 200,000-artifact instance, 340 took about 0.9 seconds, the exclusive-lock window about 0.8 seconds, and a concurrent `artifacts` read waited 0.5 seconds. Like 339 it waits at most 5 seconds per attempt, five attempts in about 35 seconds; unlike 339 it also retries a deadlock; if all fail the server exits with nothing of 340 applied and the next start retries it.
- **341 builds `idx_sync_tasks_artifact_id` `CONCURRENTLY`** (#5624; 37 ms on the same instance), so a deleted artifact no longer scans `sync_tasks` for its foreign-key action. It has the same long-transaction caveat as the other concurrent builds below.
- **337 and 338 add MCP introspection job columns** (#5463, #5465): the gate-release bookkeeping for jobs handed back to the queue, and `claimed_by_user_id`, which binds a claim to the worker that took it. Both are additive.
- **Concurrent index builds.** 297, 313, 315, 335, 336 and 341 build indexes `CONCURRENTLY` (download-statistics checksum and retention indexes, MCP introspection and tombstone indexes, the `sync_tasks` artifact index); 296, 312 and 314 first drop any invalid leftover of an interrupted build. **A concurrent build waits for every transaction already open on the database, on any table** (a `pg_dump`, a reporting query, an idle-in-transaction session). The migration logs nothing while it waits, and the Helm chart's startupProbe (30 × 5 s) restarts the pod until that transaction ends; the next start then completes the migration (#5613). End or wait out long transactions before the first 1.12.0 replica starts.
- **Backfills.** 290 marks every existing age-gate decision and configured policy as instance-locked (#4238; see below). 317 turns existing acknowledged findings into acknowledgement decisions in its own migration, so nothing is locked across that scan of `scan_findings` (#5153). **It skips acknowledgements that a decision could turn into a hidden open finding**, and those findings show as open after the upgrade: one acknowledged only in an older scan and reported open by the current one, one engine's row acknowledged while another engine's row for the same identity is open, and one acknowledged in a scan the artifact no longer reports it in (#5614). An acknowledged finding that reopens also brings back any scan-policy hold its acknowledgement had released. Find them with `SELECT sf.id FROM scan_findings sf JOIN scan_findings_effective e ON e.id = sf.id WHERE sf.is_acknowledged AND NOT e.is_acknowledged;` and acknowledge them again with a `repository_id`, which covers every engine. 298, 308, 311 and 323 seed their new conda shard, RPM repodata and MCP tables from existing rows.
- **Short catalog locks.** 295, 298, 299, 301, 303, 307, 308, 309, 311, 318, 323 and 328 change existing tables under a 5-second `lock_timeout`.
- **330** changes the default replication mode of a peer subscription from `pull` (never implemented) to `push` (#5293, also in 1.11.12).

**Mixed 1.11/1.12 fleets** behave as follows until every replica is on 1.12.0:

- A scan-policy hold answers `403` on 1.12 replicas and the old `409` on 1.11 replicas (#4510).
- The new instance lock on a repository's proxy scan policy is not enforced by 1.11 replicas, which accept a repository administrator's weakening write (#4363). Finish the upgrade before relying on it.
- A lifecycle policy that uses the new `match.format` scope is refused by 1.11 replicas with `400 unknown key 'match.format'`, and a scheduled run there fails before deleting anything, so the policy only runs on upgraded replicas (#2024).
- Migration 316 freezes the old `scan_findings.is_acknowledged` columns and 1.12 no longer reads them, so an acknowledgement change made on a 1.11 replica after the first 1.12 replica migrated, an acknowledgement or a revoke alike, does not reach 1.12; redo those changes on 1.12 after the rollout (#5153, #5614). The same holds for changes made on 1.11 after a rollback.
- **A 1.11 replica that restarts after the first 1.12 replica has migrated exits with `Migration(VersionMissing(290))` and crash-loops** until the rollout replaces it. Finish the rollout, or set `SKIP_MIGRATIONS=true` on the old ReplicaSet.
- A 1.11 replica that purges an artifact after 340 has run leaves the peer-delete task without a target address (1.11 never writes the new columns, and the foreign key now sets `artifact_id` to `NULL`), so that delete is never sent to push peers. Run purges from 1.12 replicas during the rollout (#5624).
- OCI manifest reads by digest move onto the `oci_manifests` table (#1683, #4955). While 1.11 replicas still run, keep `BLOB_GC_ENABLED` unset and `GC_TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS` above the rollout length on them; `docs/operations/oci-manifests-reconcile.md` has a table of what a mixed fleet answers.

**Rolling back.** A plain 1.11.12 image started on the migrated database fails safely: it exits with `Migration(VersionMissing(290))` and changes nothing. Rolling back with `SKIP_MIGRATIONS=true` on the 1.11.12 deployment works, and rolling forward again is clean. `docs/operations/rollback.md` has the procedure.

### New and changed settings

- **`PROXY_UPSTREAM_MAX_DETACHED_FILLS`** (default 16 per replica) bounds proxy cache fills that outlive their request (#5220, #5509). A buffered cold fetch whose client disconnects keeps running and fills the cache (#5220, also in 1.11.13). In 1.12.0 the same slots also cover **streamed fills whose client stopped reading**: a ranged `GET` whose window ends before the end of the file, or a client that disconnects mid-stream. Such a fill reads the rest of the object on its own task and commits it, so the next request is a cache hit (#5509). A detached fill is abandoned `PROXY_UPSTREAM_FETCH_DEADLINE_SECS` plus 60 seconds after it detaches; for a streamed fill that clock starts when the client drops (#5617). With no slot free, a fill ends with its client, as before. Related: `PROXY_UPSTREAM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS`, `PROXY_UPSTREAM_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS` (#5220) and `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_LOCK_MAX_CONNECTIONS` (default `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_MAX_LOCK_WAITERS` + 1, #5475).
- **Proxy and Remotes:** `PROXY_UPSTREAM_MODE` and the per-Remote `upstream_mode` (`cache_only`, #5282), `PROXY_STALE_IF_ERROR_GRACE_SECS` (#4581), `AZURE_PROXY_CACHE_ENABLED` (#4320), `AK_UPSTREAM_ENV_PROXY` (#5459, see below), `AK_PROXY_SCAN_QUEUE_BUDGET_BYTES` and `AK_PROXY_SCAN_QUEUE_WAIT_SECS` (#5231), `AK_SERVE_VERIFY_BUFFER_BUDGET_BYTES` (#5064), `MAX_NPM_IDENTITY_ARCHIVE_ENTRIES` (#5148).
- **Disconnected operation:** `UPSTREAM_JOBS_PAUSED` (#5288), `CURATION_POPULARITY_NPM_URL` / `CURATION_POPULARITY_PYPI_URL` (the download-count API used by curation popularity rules: an internal mirror of the same API, or `off`; #5288), `AUDIT_UPSTREAM_FETCHES` (`off`, `errors`, `all`; #5286), and for the scanner adapter `SCANNER_OFFLINE`, `SCANNER_ADAPTER_TOKEN` and `SCANNER_TRIVY_SKIP_DB_UPDATE`, which now also applies to filesystem scans (#5287).
- **Auth:** `DEVICE_AUTH_ENABLED` (off by default, #3461), `LDAP_BASIC_AUTH_PASSTHROUGH` (off by default, #3830), `SESSION_REVOCATION_CACHE_TTL_SECS` (default 5, #4883), and a `<NAME>_FILE` companion for every credential-typed setting (`DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET`, `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, `LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD`, `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AZURE_STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY` and the rest; #4142). A `_FILE` that points at an unreadable or empty file stops startup with an error naming the variable and the path.
- **Storage and GC:** `STORAGE_GC_DELETE_CONCURRENCY` (default 4) and the per-pass budgets `STORAGE_GC_MAX_KEYS_PER_RUN`, `STORAGE_GC_MAX_BYTES_PER_RUN` and `STORAGE_GC_MAX_RUN_SECS` (#2524), `S3_MAX_PARTS` (#4805), `AZURE_COPY_TIMEOUT_SECS` (minimum deadline for one server-side Put Blob From URL copy; unset, 60 s plus the source size at 8 MiB/s; #4858), `OCI_MANIFESTS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECS` (default 21600, #4955), `DOWNLOAD_STATS_RETENTION_DAYS` and `DOWNLOAD_STATS_RETENTION_INTERVAL_SECS` (#4541).
- **Formats:** `AK_CONDA_REGEN_CONCURRENCY`, `AK_CONDA_REGEN_WAIT_SECS`, `AK_CONDA_JLAP_REVISIONS` and `CONDA_PACKAGE_DB_WAIT_MS` (#4176, #4175, #4182), `RPM_REPODATA_BUILD_QUIET_SECS` and `RPM_REPODATA_BUILD_MAX_DELAY_SECS` (#4544), `TERRAFORM_DEFAULT_REPO` (#4356).
- **Observability:** `DB_QUERY_SPANS` (#3954) and the OTLP logs and metrics exporters, `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` and their endpoints (#4337).
- **MCP sandbox:** `AK_MCP_SANDBOX_RUNTIME`, `AK_MCP_SANDBOX_NETWORK`, `AK_MCP_SANDBOX_GATEWAY`, `AK_MCP_SANDBOX_AK_HOST` / `AK_MCP_SANDBOX_AK_IP`, `AK_MCP_INTROSPECTOR_TOKEN_FILE` and the related settings in `docs/mcp-registry.md` (#5384, #5385, #5390, #5447).

### Behaviour changes operators will notice

- **A write refused to a caller who cannot read the repository now answers the unknown-key `404`, on every format** (#5458). Before, an authenticated caller who could not read a private repository got `403` (or a wrong-type `400`) for an existing key and `404` for a missing one, which let any authenticated caller enumerate private repository keys. Native format routes answer `404 Repository not found` (the MCP registry its unknown-name problem+json), REST routes under `/api/v1/repositories/{key}` answer `404`, including the admin-tier configuration reads that run the write or admin gate (`GET .../age-gate`, the age-gate review queue, `GET .../npm-scope-policy`, `GET .../egress-proxy`), and OCI `/v2` pushes and deletes answer `404 NAME_UNKNOWN`. Docker-mirror mode (`AK_DEFAULT_DOCKER_MIRROR_REPO`) no longer redirects a push to an unknown key to the mirror. **A caller who can read the repository but not write it still gets `403`**, as does any caller on a `public` repository and any authenticated caller on an `internal` one, except a token scoped elsewhere. **If a publish or CI push starts failing with `404` after the upgrade, check the token's repository scope and the caller's grants before checking the key's spelling.** `docs/repository-visibility.md` has a troubleshooting section.
- **Virtual repositories answer `503` with `Retry-After` when a member is temporarily unavailable and nothing else serves the file, and `404` for a member's permanent upstream `4xx`** (#5504, #5495). A member counts as unavailable for an upstream `5xx`, `408`, `425` or `429`, a timeout or a transport failure; the walk passes over it as over a missing one and still serves from a lower-priority member that has the file. **This applies to artifact downloads**: generic downloads, Maven artifacts and checksums, npm tarballs, Cargo crates, Conda packages, Alpine `.apk` files and VS Code extension downloads, across the shared artifact walk (Maven, sbt, npm, Cargo, Conda, Debian, Go, Composer, Hex, Alpine, Chef, Git LFS, JetBrains, Protobuf, Terraform, VS Code, the generic `/download/` and `/general/` routes) and the scan-aware walks of Cargo, Conda, VS Code, Conan, CocoaPods, Pub, Swift and RubyGems. **Metadata and index lookups still answer `404` during a member outage**: the npm packument, the PyPI simple index and PyPI files, the Cargo index, Helm chart archives, and OCI manifests, blobs and tags (#5620, #5621). Maven metadata is the exception: Maven metadata (`maven-metadata.xml` and its checksums) through a Virtual where no member serves and at least one is unavailable (5xx, 408/425/429, DNS/connect/TLS failure or connect timeout) now answers `503` with `Retry-After` and is not cached, instead of a cacheable `404`; 1.11.x answered `502` naming the member when the upstream was blackholed and `404` otherwise. A member that misses the 20 s deadline still gets the `502` (#5669). A Remote member whose upstream answers `403` for a missing key (S3-hosted Maven buckets) or `401` for stale credentials no longer turns every missing `.sha1` into a `503` that clients retry forever. A member's quarantine or policy block, and a Maven or Go member's age refusal (`451`), still take precedence over a `503`. **Expect `503` where clients used to see a `404` that Gradle cached**, during upstream outages.
- **`Range` is honoured on the generic route's Remote and Virtual serves** (#5502), the Alpine package route (#5478, #5509) and Hugging Face `resolve` (#5145), through one shared helper: `206` with `Content-Range`, `416` for an unsatisfiable range, `If-Range` honoured, and a `HEAD` with `Range` answered `200` without a body. `Range` is still never sent upstream, so a cold serve fills the cache with the whole object, and a ranged cold fetch now actually fills it (#5509).
- **A download refused by a scan-policy hold answers `403`, not `409`** (#4510). Upload-period and administrator holds still answer `409`. Treat `403` on a held artifact as final until the findings are resolved.
- **A quarantined or rejected OCI image stays refused when its tag moves** (#5457). Every manifest read checks every live row of the digest, and a push that moves a held tag moves the hold to the old digest's row. **Releasing acts on one row**, so a held image stays refused until every held row of its digest is released; there is no "release this digest everywhere" action yet. A rejected image whose tag moved away keeps a live digest row until an administrator deletes it. See `docs/security/download-holds.md`.
- **Restoring a trashed artifact cancels its queued peer deletes and pushes it again** (#5505, #5497) for every eligible push or mirror peer. A delete for a peer the restore does not push to (a pull-mode subscriber, a peer a sync policy now excludes, a disabled subscription) is kept, so that peer still drops the artifact. A delete made while a peer was offline is now replicated when it returns (#5497).
- **Scan findings with long version or source strings are stored** (#5534, migration 339). A finding that still cannot be stored (a NUL byte, or a `cve_id` over 30 characters) fails only its own scanner's result, with an error naming the finding and the column, and the other scanners for the artifact still run. The `source` findings filter accepts up to 1024 characters.
- **Scan-on-proxy now enforces for Go, RubyGems, Composer, Pub, Conan, CocoaPods, Swift, Debian, RPM and Alpine Remotes and Virtuals that already had it enabled** (#4103, #4104, #4105, #4107, #4108, #4109, #4110, #4111, #4112, #4113). These pulls streamed unscanned before, so a gate that was never exercised can start answering `403 scan_blocked`, or `423` under `fail_closed`. Archives are also graded as the version requested, not only on what they bundle (#4952).
- **`DELETE /api/v1/repositories/{key}` answers `202` with a job** (#4311) instead of deleting in the request; the key stops resolving at once and can be reused. Clients that expect `200` must accept `202`. Progress is at `GET /api/v1/repository-deletions/{id}`. **ak CLI 1.2.0 and earlier report an error on `ak repo delete` against 1.12.0 although the delete succeeded; upgrade to ak 1.11.0 or later.**
- **Peer links must use an administrator token with the `admin` scope on the receiving side** (#5455). The `x-artifact-keeper-replication: true` header now counts only with such a token. A link whose `api_key` is a service-account token, or an administrator token without `admin`, replicates as an ordinary writer: its mirrored deletes of released artifacts get `409`, and writes over a quota `413`/`507`. Re-issue the key and restrict it to the replicated repositories.
- **Destinations reached through `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` are checked against the outbound address policy** (#5459). Internal mirrors and private storage endpoints (for example Azure Private Link) reached through a corporate proxy are refused unless `UPSTREAM_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS` or `AK_SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS` admits them, and the backend now resolves proxied host names itself. Where it can reach DNS only through the proxy, give it a resolver or set `AK_UPSTREAM_ENV_PROXY=ignore`.
- **Age-gate decisions and policies from before the upgrade are instance-locked** (#4238, migration 290). Repository admins can now operate their own repository's age gate; hand an existing policy to its team with `"instance_locked": false`.
- **Webhooks.** The legacy `X-Webhook-Signature` header is now `sha256=HMAC(secret, body)`, as documented (#5234). A receiver written against the old value, computed over `"<t>.<body>"`, fails after the upgrade; verify the `v1=` token in `X-ArtifactKeeper-Signature` instead. `POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret` returns the new secret once (#5235).
- **Smaller changes.** Signing out invalidates the session's access token too, on other replicas within `SESSION_REVOCATION_CACHE_TTL_SECS` (#4883). Per-repository settings reads (`cache-ttl`, `on-upstream-not-found`, `stale-if-error-grace`, `routing-rules`, `pypi-tracks`) answer `404` to a caller who cannot read the repository (#4815). Creating a repository with upstream credentials but no `upstream_auth_type` answers `400` instead of dropping them (#4825). Repository security `grade` is nullable and never the F floor; read `grade_status` (#4336). Every outbound HTTP client sends `User-Agent: artifact-keeper/<version>` (#5110). The Incus native chunked upload routes carry `Deprecation` headers pointing at `/api/v1/uploads` (#5002). A Maven `.md5`, `.sha1` or `.sha256` upload must name the stored artifact's digest (`400` otherwise), and replacing a released artifact's stored sidecar answers `409`; a normal deploy is unaffected (#5665).

### Image changes

- **Backend image:** bundled `grype` moves to v0.121.3, and `buildctl` (still BuildKit v0.33.1) is rebuilt with `golang.org/x/net` v0.62.0, clearing CVE-2026-78661 and every HIGH and CRITICAL finding in the 1.11.12 image (#5565). `.trivyignore` has no live suppressions any more. The image builds with jemalloc (#5130).
- **Scanner adapter 1.7.0:** its `trivy` moves to `ghcr.io/artifact-keeper/trivy:0.76.0-r4`, the unchanged Trivy 0.76.0 source rebuilt with `x/net` v0.62.0 (#5571), so a self-run Trivy server stays on 0.76.0. It gains offline mode and the `PUT /api/v1/vulndb` import route (#5287).

### Known issues and follow-ups

- On the virtual **artifact** walk, a hosted member whose storage read fails still reads as a miss (`404`), while the checksum walk answers `503` (#5574, 1.13.0).
- `scan_results.scanner_version` and `vuln_db_version` are still `VARCHAR`, so an over-long value can strand a scan in `running` the way #5534 did (#5564, 1.13.0).
- The MCP backing gate's Virtual shadowing check does not model per-caller member visibility (#5536), and `held_backing_package` locks alias rows without rechecking their checksum across a tag move (#5593); both 1.13.0.
- The generic `/download` route answers `502` for a docker repository's manifest even with no hold (#5594, 1.13.0).
- `docker push` cannot replace a tag held by a scan policy or quarantine: the pull gate also refuses docker's pre-push `HEAD`/`GET` of the manifest, so docker never sends the `PUT`. Push under a new tag, release the hold, or delete the manifest first (#5606).
- A hold placed while a push is moving the tag, where the push takes the tag row first, lands on the new image: the old digest stays servable and the new one is held (#5646).
- Adding a label to an artifact deletes it from peers that received it through a manual subscription (`POST /api/v1/peers/{id}/repositories`) (#5625).
- A "full" backup omits Docker/OCI images (and groups, webhooks, settings and scan data), and restoring a deleted Docker repository reports success while the image answers `404` (#5654).
- A storage outage (S3/MinIO unreachable) makes uploads and downloads hang until storage returns instead of answering `503` (#5649).
- `npm audit` through an npm Virtual answers `{}`, which npm reports as 0 vulnerabilities (#5631).
- The MCP introspection worker's stdio sandbox does not apply the response-integrity checks of #5450: a wrong JSON-RPC id ends in a 120-second timeout, and duplicate responses pass (#5636).
- Basic auth with an API token as the password costs a bcrypt check per request, which can exhaust the authentication limiter (`503`) under package-manager bursts; send the token as `Bearer` (#5640).

## MCP Registry

- **Hosted registries** (#5253). A Local or Staging `mcp` repository speaks the MCP registry API v0.1 (and `/v0`) at `/mcp/{repo}/`, so VS Code's MCP gallery, GitHub Copilot's private registry policy and `mcp-publisher` can use it in place of the public registry. Under the default `mcp_package_policy: own-repos`, every package a server runs must already be in one of this instance's repositories; the publish pins the exact version or image digest and reads serve the Artifact Keeper coordinates. Versions are write-once and stay reserved after deletion; MCPB bundles are hosted; lint rolls up each version's health.
- **Remote and Virtual registries** (#5253). A Remote is an approval-gated allowlist populated from an upstream registry, can be seeded with named versions without a full catalog sync (#5408), and syncs in the background with `202` (#5404, #5422). A Virtual merges members, and `mcp-publisher` can log in with GitHub Actions OIDC under per-namespace publish grants.
- **Introspection.** Capability snapshots and tool diffs come from an isolated introspection worker that runs each server in a gVisor or Kata sandbox with enforced time, memory, disk and failure bounds; rootless Podman guests can no longer reach each other (#5384, #5390, #5447). Results are refused when they break protocol integrity (worker answer `refused` with `details.protocolViolation`, #5450), or come from the wrong claimant or an expired lease (`409 mcp_claim_invalid`, #5461, #5462, #5465), or when their observation or cache metadata is out of bounds (`400 mcp_invalid_result_metadata`, which replaces `mcp_invalid_capabilities` for that case, on job completion and on CI/gateway capability reports alike; #5466, #5543). A job whose serve gate cannot be evaluated is handed back to the queue with a backoff, and a claim answers `503 mcp_gate_unavailable` only when nothing servable was found; a completion that hits the same outage answers `503` and leaves the claim as it was (#5463, migration 337).
- **Sandbox jobs are strict.** An npm or PyPI job that could make `npx` / `uvx` install from anywhere but the serving repository is refused as `unsupported` (#5446). An OCI job needs a canonical, digest-pinned reference that round-trips, on the job's own Artifact Keeper origin with an exact host and port; a bare dotless, port-less base URL is refused, so give the instance a domain name or a port. An OCI package's `runtimeArguments` are dropped with a note (#5448).
- **Shadowing.** An approved version is pinned to what its Virtual backing repository actually serves (#5456). A publish a Remote member would shadow answers `422 mcp_package_shadowed`. **On upgrade, existing approved versions are checked too:** versions pinned through an npm or NuGet Virtual with a Remote member ranked above the hosted member, and through a PyPI Virtual with any Remote member that has an upstream, are held as soon as they are read (`404 mcp_unresolvable`, `gate: shadowed` for the holder) and drop out of listings and `latest`. Re-rank the hosted member above the Remote, turn on isolate mode on the npm Virtual, or remove the Remote from the PyPI Virtual, and the hold clears on the next read without a republish.
- **Bundles and URLs.** MCPB uploads enforce the shared archive entry ceiling and refuse ambiguous or unsafe entries with `400 mcp_bundle_invalid` (#5467, #5469). A templated remote or package transport URL is checked for what it expands to and refused with `400 mcp_invalid_server_json`; the lint rule set is `ak-mcp-lint/3` (#5529).
- **Disclosure.** Listings, search, the storage tree and the generic read routes no longer reveal server versions a reader is not served; listing cursors carry an opaque row id instead of a name or version (#5338, #5391, #5428, #5429, #5453), and `/api/v1/packages` hides soft-deleted MCP versions (#5454). An administrator purge removes a deleted version for good (#5368).

## Disconnected and air-gapped operation

`docs/air-gapped.md` and `docs/operations/disconnected-operation.md` tie these together (#5293, #5369):

- **Cache-only Remotes** serve every cached entry, fresh or stale, and answer a miss with `404 ... is cache-only` without contacting the upstream (#5282); a config export carries the mode (#5407).
- **Proxy-cache seeding** from a list of paths, as a resumable background job with a per-path inventory (#5284).
- **An `UPSTREAM_FETCHED` audit trail** of every request the proxy sends upstream (#5286, #5347).
- **One switch pauses every scheduled job that contacts an upstream** (#5288).
- **The scanner adapter runs offline** and imports a trivy DB over HTTP without a restart (#5287).
- **Repository config export, plan and apply** between instances, with credentials replaced by `secret_ref` placeholders (#5292).
- A Go Remote caches the checksum database, so `go` verifies seeded modules with the checksum database out of reach (#5344).

## Security

- **Existence oracles closed.** Refused writes (#5458) and per-repository settings reads (#4815) no longer tell a private repository from an unknown key; see the upgrade notes.
- **Replication and peers.** The replication header grants nothing without an instance administrator's token (#5455).
- **Outbound requests.** Proxied destinations are checked against the outbound address policy (#5459).
- **Sessions.** Logout and refresh-token replay detection invalidate the access token (#4883).
- **Holds.** OCI holds follow the digest across tag moves and aliases (#5457), and an administrator's quarantine or rejection that commits while a push is moving the tag is no longer lost (#5618).
- **Repository visibility on the new routes.** The proxy-cache cap routes and the virtual member listing answer a caller who cannot read a private repository the unknown-key `404` (#5610, #5612).
- **Peers.** Purging an artifact, deleting it with `?permanent=true` or deleting its repository now removes it from push and mirror peers too, instead of leaving it served there (#5624, migrations 340 and 341).
- **MCP.** The hardening above, plus Unicode linting of resources, prompts and instructions (#5388), case-insensitive shadowing and case-only twin refusal (#5394, #5434), equal gate work for held and missing versions (#5396), administrator-only MCP settings (#5398), and a repository-scoped introspection token that can no longer claim another repository's jobs (#5460).
- **Dependencies.** zip 9.1.2 for GHSA-m665-v7pm-7grj (critical; #5026, shipped in 1.11.x as #5441), wasmtime 36.0.20, rustls-webpki 0.103.16, ctutils 0.4.5, crypto-bigint 0.7.6, zstd 0.14.3, pulldown-cmark 0.13.6, libz-sys and the other RUSTSEC bumps shipped on 1.11.x are all here; the Go toolchain floor and go-jose 4.1.6 for the bundled Go tools (#4852, #5041). `cargo audit` ignores RUSTSEC-2026-0459 with a justification: the advisory is in `libsqlite3-sys`, which `sqlx-sqlite` names in `Cargo.lock` but which the backend never builds or links (#5555).
- The security advisories published since 1.11.3 cover fixes that shipped in 1.11.4 to 1.11.10; all of them are in 1.12.0.

## Proxy, virtual repositories and storage

- **Remote behaviour.** `on_upstream_not_found = keep` keeps serving a cached copy when the upstream answers `404`/`410` (#4640); stale-if-error serves are marked and the grace period is configurable (#4581); a proxy-cache cap in bytes with LRU eviction (#4660); the proxy cache on Azure Blob storage (#4320); a cold `HEAD` no longer downloads the file (#5322, #5343); fills of a disconnected client complete (#5220, #5509); Remote OCI repositories repair a corrupt stored blob from upstream (#5169).
- **Virtual correctness.** Member failures and misses (#5504, #5495); Composer Virtuals serve Packagist-style Remote members (#4951); NuGet V3 search aggregates V2 remotes and follows continuation pages (#4976, #4856); Maven `X-Checksum-SHA1` through virtuals (#4573, #4963); Maven metadata through a Virtual whose members are unavailable answers `503` with `Retry-After` instead of a cacheable `404` (#5669).
- **Storage.** GC without a transaction across object-store deletes, with budgets and metrics (#2524); chunked and single-PUT uploads streamed into object storage instead of local scratch (#3916, #4990, #5002); S3 multipart part budget for stores capped at 1,000 parts (#4805); bounded serve-time verification (#5064); TCP_NODELAY on accepted connections, which removes a 44 ms delay on small keep-alive downloads (#5139). On S3, GCS and Azure storage, new Git LFS objects are now stored under a repository-scoped key, so pushing an object another repository already holds (a fork or mirror) no longer fails with `409 CONFLICT`; existing objects keep serving from their recorded key and no migration is needed (#5659). On 1.11.x two repositories pushing the same LFS object silently shared one stored copy. On S3, GCS and Azure storage, new MCP server versions and MCPB bundles are now stored under a repository-scoped key, and an approval or pin whose ingested version cannot be stored now answers `409`, `507` or `500` (the decision still stands and the next sync retries); existing objects are unchanged and no migration is needed (#5660).
- **Formats.** Hosted conda repodata rendered once per change, stored CEP-16 shards, JLAP and backpressure (#4173, #4174, #4175, #4176); synthesised shards for Remotes without a shard index (#4178); precomputed hosted RPM repodata with `repodata_mode` and a rebuild endpoint (#4544); hosted Terraform as an OpenTofu/Terraform origin registry (#4356) and presigned network-mirror redirects (#5015); the Maven age gate (#4702); Hugging Face streaming uploads, `Range` and commit-pinned caching (#5291, #5145, #5283); model-file scanning for `huggingface` and `mlmodel` (#5285).

## Auth, administration and observability

- **Sign-in.** RFC 8628 device authorization (#3461), LDAP/AD Basic passthrough on package routes (#3830), pre-provisioned OIDC groups (#4297), `<NAME>_FILE` secrets (#4142).
- **Administration.** Repository admins operate their own age gate (#4238); instance locks on proxy scan policies (#4363); durable finding acknowledgements, which also release a scan-policy hold when the last open finding is acknowledged (#5153); a policy-blocks queue (#4510) and what-would-block previews for `record_only` (#5232); permanent delete from trash (#4700); hidden web UI navigation entries (#4574); group member listing (#4027); the relay `PATCH` route (#4795).
- **Observability.** OTLP logs and metrics (#4337, #4931); database and upstream client spans (#3954); repository metadata render metrics (#4923); proxy cache publish failure counter (#4319); `docs/operations/tracing.md` and `logging.md` (#4960).

## Other repositories

- **artifact-keeper-web:** web 1.12.0 is released alongside this backend and is required with it (see the upgrade notes, #5663).
- **artifact-keeper-iac (Helm chart):** the chart bump follows the release, as for 1.11.x.
- **artifact-keeper-test:** the release gate's webhook-signing suites run against a backend started with a webhook secret key and fail under `RELEASE_GATE=1` when the key is missing, instead of skipping their real checks (#5196).
